# Content review pack

**Generated by `npm run content:export` -- do not hand-edit.** This pack reflects the content files at the time it was generated; regenerate it before review. Review the wording below and send feedback to the project lead. Once approved, the files in `content/` get `status: approved`, `reviewed_by` (role only) and `reviewed_on`.

For each item please say: approve, or what to change.

## canopy (status: draft)

### What this means

Tree canopy cover is the share of the land that is shaded by the leaves and branches of trees when you look down from above.

Trees take in carbon dioxide, cool hot streets, soak up heavy rain and give homes to birds, insects and other wildlife. A higher share is better.

This figure comes from a survey of the whole local ward, so it is an estimate for the parish, not a count of trees. Where the survey only covers one year, the dashboard cannot yet show whether cover is going up or down.

### Opportunities

- [Free trees for communities](https://www.woodlandtrust.org.uk/plant-trees/schools-and-communities/) (Woodland Trust): The Woodland Trust gives community groups free trees and advice on planting them. A parish group could apply for a pack. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Join the local environment champions](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/p/community-groups/cholsey-environment-champions/) (Cholsey Environment Champions (Low Carbon Hub)): Cholsey Environment Champions are a local climate and nature group with a wildlife activity area. Ask them how to help with local planting. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Grants to plant woodland on farm or estate land](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/england-woodland-creation-offer) (Forestry Commission (GOV.UK)): If you own or manage land, the England Woodland Creation Offer pays towards planting new woodland. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

## electricity (status: draft)

### What this means

This shows how much electricity the average home meter uses in a year. It is measured in kilowatt hours, or kWh. One kWh runs a one-bar electric heater for an hour.

Using less electricity saves money and cuts carbon, especially when the grid still burns some gas. A lower figure is better. Moving heating and cars to electricity will push the figure up. So the long-term goal is cleaner electricity, not just less.

Parish figures are worked out from small neighbourhood areas that only partly match the parish edge, so they are estimates.

### Opportunities

- [Advice on making your home cosier](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/?p=7175) (Low Carbon Hub): Cosy Homes Oxfordshire gives independent advice on insulation, heating and other upgrades, with real examples of Oxfordshire homes. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Retrofit support from the district council](https://www.southoxon.gov.uk/south-oxfordshire-district-council/tackling-the-climate-emergency/what-can-you-do/retrofitting-your-home) (South Oxfordshire District Council): South Oxfordshire District Council explains how to retrofit a home and where to find funding. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Find ways to save energy at home](https://www.gov.uk/improve-energy-efficiency) (GOV.UK): The government's energy efficiency tool suggests improvements for your home and points to grants you may be able to get. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

## gas (status: draft)

### What this means

This shows how much gas the average home meter uses in a year, measured in kilowatt hours, or kWh. Most of it is used for heating and hot water.

Gas gives off carbon dioxide when it burns, so using less is better for the climate and for bills. The best ways to cut it are to stop heat escaping, with loft and wall insulation, and later to swap a gas boiler for a heat pump.

Gas use changes with the weather and with energy prices, so a cold winter or a price rise can move the figure. Parish figures are estimates made from small neighbourhood areas.

### Opportunities

- [Find ways to save energy at home](https://www.gov.uk/improve-energy-efficiency) (GOV.UK): The government's energy efficiency tool suggests improvements, such as insulation, and points to any grants you may be able to get. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Retrofit support from the district council](https://www.southoxon.gov.uk/south-oxfordshire-district-council/tackling-the-climate-emergency/what-can-you-do/retrofitting-your-home) (South Oxfordshire District Council): South Oxfordshire District Council explains how to retrofit a home and where to find funding. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Whole-house advice](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/?p=7175) (Low Carbon Hub): Cosy Homes Oxfordshire offers independent retrofit advice and a whole-house assessment service, which may carry a fee. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

## greenspace (status: draft)

### What this means

Accessible green space is land the public can use, such as parks, playing fields, play areas and sports facilities. The dashboard shows how much there is for each resident.

Green space helps people stay active, meet neighbours and feel calmer. It also gives wildlife room to live and helps soak up rain. A higher figure is better.

We add up mapped sites that the public can use inside the parish. The map data leaves out open countryside and common land. We also do not count allotments, churchyards, cemeteries or golf courses. So the figure is more likely to be too low than too high. We do not measure how good a site is, or how easy it is to get to from your front door.

### Opportunities

- [Protect a favourite green space](https://www.fieldsintrust.org/) (Fields in Trust): Fields in Trust helps communities give their local parks and playing fields lasting legal protection. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Volunteer for local wildlife](https://www.bbowt.org.uk/) (BBOWT): The Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust runs volunteer work parties and events on nature reserves across the area. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Join the wildlife group in Cholsey](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/p/community-groups/cholsey-environment-champions/) (Cholsey Environment Champions (Low Carbon Hub)): Cholsey Environment Champions have a wildlife group. Find out how to join in. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

## heat_pump (status: draft)

### What this means

A heat pump heats a home by moving heat from the air or ground outside. It uses much less energy than a gas boiler for the same warmth, and it can run on clean electricity.

This shows the share of homes with a heat pump installed by a certified installer. A higher share is better, because heat pumps are the main way to stop heating homes with gas.

The source only counts installations certified under the MCS scheme. It reports for the whole South Oxfordshire district. Where the Cholsey figure is marked as an estimate, it is based on the district rate. In that case it cannot show how Cholsey differs from its neighbours.

### Opportunities

- [Government grant for a heat pump](https://www.gov.uk/apply-boiler-upgrade-scheme) (GOV.UK): The Boiler Upgrade Scheme gives a grant towards the cost of a heat pump for eligible homes in England. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Find a certified installer](https://www.mcscertified.com/find-an-installer/) (MCS): Use the MCS directory to find heat pump installers who meet the national standard. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Independent retrofit advice](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/?p=7175) (Low Carbon Hub): Cosy Homes Oxfordshire can help you work out whether a heat pump suits your home and what to do first. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

## solar_pv (status: draft)

### What this means

Solar PV panels turn sunlight into electricity. This shows the share of homes that have panels installed by a certified installer.

More panels mean more clean power made close to where it is used. A higher share is better.

The source only counts installations certified under the MCS scheme, so older or uncertified systems are missed. It reports for the whole South Oxfordshire district. Where the Cholsey figure is marked as an estimate, it is based on the district rate. In that case it cannot show how Cholsey differs from its neighbours.

### Opportunities

- [Get paid for the power you export](https://www.gov.uk/feed-in-tariffs/smart-export-guarantee) (GOV.UK): Under the Smart Export Guarantee, energy suppliers pay you for extra solar electricity you send back to the grid. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Find a certified installer](https://www.mcscertified.com/find-an-installer/) (MCS): Use the MCS directory to find installers who meet the national standard. _Last checked 2026-10-03._
- [Community-owned solar](https://www.lowcarbonhub.org/) (Low Carbon Hub): Low Carbon Hub helps Oxfordshire communities set up and share in local renewable energy projects. _Last checked 2026-10-03._

**Feedback:** 

## About page (status: draft)

This dashboard shows how Cholsey is doing on trees, green space, home energy and the move to cleaner heating. It compares the parish with nearby parishes, South Oxfordshire and England, and links each measure to things you can do.

Every number comes from public open data, and each one can be traced to its source. Select the source line under any figure to see who published it, which area and year it covers, and how it was worked out. Figures marked as estimates have been calculated for the parish from data published for other areas.

The dashboard is a community project and is not an official statement by Cholsey Parish Council. The wording on the pages is a draft until it has been reviewed.

The code, data and decisions behind the dashboard are open and can be read on GitHub. If you spot a mistake, please open an issue there.

**Feedback:** 

## Glossary (status: draft)

- **Tree canopy cover**: The share of land shaded by tree leaves and branches when seen from above.
- **Accessible green space**: Mapped parks, playing fields, play areas and similar sites that the public can use.
- **kWh (kilowatt hour)**: A unit of energy. One kWh runs a one-bar electric heater for an hour.
- **Meter**: A household electricity or gas supply point. Consumption figures are given per meter.
- **Solar PV**: Panels that turn sunlight into electricity.
- **Heat pump**: A device that heats a home by moving heat from the air or ground outside.
- **MCS**: The Microgeneration Certification Scheme, a national standard for small renewable energy installers. Its records are the source for solar and heat pump counts.
- **Parish estimate**: A figure for Cholsey worked out from data published for a different area, such as a ward, a group of small neighbourhoods or the whole district. It is flagged wherever it appears.
- **Comparator**: A nearby parish shown beside Cholsey so you can see how it compares.
- **District**: South Oxfordshire, the local council area that Cholsey belongs to.
- **Latest available**: The most recent year the source has published. It is often older than the current year, and the year is always shown.
- **Better, similar, worse**: Whether Cholsey is clearly better, within a small margin of, or clearly worse than another area, taking into account whether a higher or lower figure is good for that measure.
- **Open Government Licence**: The licence that lets anyone reuse most UK public sector data, as long as the source is credited.
